about: CHAIN dirham_hoard (Design/content/chains/dirham_hoard.md): a dying Gotlander's account of silver buried on his farm, and the kin who also know. Fourteen cards, 805 to 950. A Gotland trader dies of a fever in a western harbour and tells a stranger with a boat where his silver lies: one lot under his storehouse floor, which his brother and his daughter each half know of, and a greater lot under the stern stone of an old ship of stones in his pasture, which nobody knows of. The merchant carries the word to Gotland, sees the first lot dug and quarrelled over, stands witness at the thing, and then decides what becomes of the second. Five endings: the daughter has it (end_daughter); the brother has it and lays it back in the ground (end_brother); it is left under the stone and never dug (end_buried: what really happened to hundreds of Gotland hoards); the merchant digs it himself by night (end_thief); or the kin are brought to put all of it into a ship and a fellowship with the Frisian house, with a booth on the beach (end_fellowship: history changed). Progress is flags ch_dirham_hoard_1 to _9; branch flags, waits, endings and grand rewards are listed in the chain page. Cards with weight 0 are reached only by 'schedule' or 'then'; the other scheduled cards also carry a weight so that a house that sails away meets them on its next call. The words are in Data/writing/chain_dirham_hoard.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text (the engine shows the effects' own facts; the outcome keys are for the integrator). Every person is invented (Gotland names from the rune stones G 111, G 113, G 280; peoples/svea_gotlandic.md). Nobody says 'dirham': it is the writing silver, the Saracens' silver. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Sliesthorp, Ripa, Birka or Dorestad in the sailing months, 805 to 949, on any call after the first). A Gotland trader lies dying of a fever in a host's house, none of his own people in harbour, and tells a stranger with a boat where his silver lies. Sources: over 700 silver hoards on Gotland, most on farms and many inside buildings (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md; economy/silver_coin.md; Ostergren 1989 (?)); the practice the game models, npc_text_encounters.md 1.5; the Saracens' silver in the Baltic from about 800 (Noonan 1998, as cited in goods_793.json); Birka men at Dorstadt (Rimbert c. 27): a Gotlander that far west is our invention (?). Hegbjorn (invented; the name from G 280). All three options hear the first measure (the storehouse floor); only the sworn man hears the second (the ship of stones). Sets ch_dirham_hoard_1; 'swear' sets ch_dirham_hoard_oath and ch_dirham_hoard_full; 'care' sets ch_dirham_hoard_cared. Schedules step 2 in three days in the same harbour.

host.note: the man in whose house he lies; invented

cards.title: A man with no kin in harbour
cards.intention: A Gotland trader lies sick of a fever in a host's back room. His ship sailed without him. He has asked the host for a man with a boat of his own, who is not of his island and not a Svea.

options.label: Give him your hand on it: his daughter shall have the word
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s01.out_swear (he tells the second measure to a sworn man only)

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s01.out_care

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s01.out_listen

memory.care: paid for a dying stranger's bed

cards.note: Step 2 (scheduled by step 1, three days later in the same harbour; a house that has sailed on never sees it and the chain goes on without it). He is dead. The host has his sea chest: a folding scale, weights, and a stick cut with runes. One of his rowers has been asking what he said. Sources: folding scales in a case and small weights as a trader's gear (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md 5); the burning of the dead as the custom of the Svear (Heimskringla, preface, tr. Laing 1844; late), and both burning and earth burial on Gotland (?); Havamal st. 77 (Bellows 1923, texts_793.json havamal_077), said at the fire by a Norse hand. The rune stick is invented. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_2; 'pyre' and 'chest' set ch_dirham_hoard_stick and ch_dirham_hoard_chest; 'pyre' sets ch_dirham_hoard_rites; 'leave' sets ch_dirham_hoard_stick_lost.

cards.title: What he left
cards.intention: The Gotlander died in the night. The host has laid him in the outhouse and put his sea chest on the table: a folding scale, a bag of weights, a comb, and a stick of yew cut with runes. He wants his lodging paid and the room back.

options.label: Pay his lodging and the wood, burn him as his people do, and take the chest for his kin
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s02.out_pyre (a Norse hand says the verse at the fire: the text goes into the chest)

options.label: Pay his lodging, take the chest for his kin, and leave the body to the host
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s02.out_chest

options.label: Leave the chest for the lodging. You carry his words, and that is enough
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s02.out_leave (the host sells the chest; the stick goes with it)

memory.leave: left a dead man's chest for the lodging

cards.note: Step 3, a side step (a crew card at sea for a house that carries the rune stick; the chain does not wait for it). The stick is read, or not. Sources: most Norse traders could read runes (npc_text_encounters.md 1.4); the sixteen runes of the younger row, one rune for several sounds; Ravn carries rune-cut sticks (spine, cast.crew.ravn); what a man buried himself he has in the next world: Snorri, Ynglinga saga c. 8 (tr. Laing 1844; late, about 1230, and Snorri's own telling (?)). Cast: cast.crew.ravn, cast.crew.aldger (if they are not aboard the forge gives two hands of their peoples). Sets ch_dirham_hoard_3; 'aloud' sets ch_dirham_hoard_full and ch_dirham_hoard_crew_knows; 'alone' may set ch_dirham_hoard_full.

cards.note: Step 4 (drawn at Paviken in the sailing months, on the first call after step 1). The beach knows the dead man, his farm, his brother and his daughter; and one of his rowers has been here asking. Sources: Paviken's shipwrights and smiths, a beach harbour with no town (ports_793.json; peoples/svea_gotlandic.md 1); the Gotlanders as farmers who are also the merchants; inheritance on Gotland by sons first and daughters where there are none, and land that stays in the kin: Guta Lag (written about 1220; late, used for custom only (?)); gifts before business (Guta saga: Ormika's twelve rams; late). Aikgard, Vivil and Ailikn are invented (names from G 280 and G 111 (?)). Sets ch_dirham_hoard_4 and one of ch_dirham_hoard_first_brother, ch_dirham_hoard_first_daughter, ch_dirham_hoard_knows_law. Schedules step 5.

cards.intention: Paviken is a beach, a row of boat sheds and the smoke of forges. You ask a shipwright for the farm called Aikgard. He puts down his adze before he answers, which is not a good sign.

memory.daughter: asked the way to the daughter

cards.note: Step 5 (scheduled by step 4, a day or two later; also drawn on any later call at Paviken). The farm, half a morning inland: the brother who holds it and the daughter who was sent for. The merchant says where the first lot lies, and to whom. Sources: the Gotland farm as an undivided holding of kin, and the daughter's right after a father with no sons (Guta Lag, late (?)); a guest is given food and drink before he is asked his errand (Havamal st. 2 to 4, texts_793.json; Guta saga). A man who gave his hand at step 1 cannot tell the brother alone: the option is greyed. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_5 and one of ch_dirham_hoard_told_daughter, ch_dirham_hoard_told_brother, ch_dirham_hoard_told_both. Schedules step 6.

cards.title: Aikgard
cards.intention: The farm lies half a morning in from the beach: a long house, a storehouse on a stone footing, sheep, and a tall stone by the gate with a ship cut on it. The brother sets ale and bread before you. The daughter has walked over from her mother's people and sits by the door.

options.label: Ask the daughter to walk with you to the gate, and tell her alone
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s05.out_tell_daughter

options.label: Tell the brother, who holds the farm and set the bread before you
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s05.out_tell_brother (a guest gift of fleeces)

options.label: Say it once, aloud, to both of them, and let them call neighbours to hear it
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s05.out_tell_both (a crock of the farm's honey)

cards.note: Step 6, the first turn (scheduled by step 5, two days later; also drawn on any later call at Paviken). The storehouse floor is taken up and the first lot is found: fifteen marks of silver, rings and cut coin, where the dead man had spoken of near forty. Sources: the Spillings hoard, 67 kg in two lots under the floor of a building, buried after 870, and with it arm rings made to a weight of about 100 g (economy/silver_coin.md; riddles_793.json rw_hoard_spillings); the mark of eight ounces, weighed, with cut and pecked coin (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md 5); a mark of about 204 g, so about 120 of Charles's pennies (?). The sizes of both lots are invented and are those of a rich farm's hoard, not of Spillings. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_6, the timer ch_dirham_hoard_wait_thing (40 days, to step 8) and the timer ch_dirham_hoard_sea_window (40 days, for step 7).

cards.intention: The storehouse boards are up. Twelve feet from the south door post, toward the tall stone, there is a flat slab, and under the slab a bronze bowl with a wooden lid. Arm rings, twisted rods, and a bag of thin coins with writing on them, many cut in half. It is a great deal of silver. It is not what he spoke of.

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s06.out_weigh (two ounces for the weigher, by both their hands)

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s06.out_stand (two cakes of the farm's wax, pressed on you at the gate)

cards.note: Step 7, a side step (a sea card in the forty days after step 6; if it never comes the chain goes on without it). The dead man's rower, with five men in a six-oared boat, thinks the Frisian carries the silver. The danger was told twice before: the host at step 2, the shipwright at step 4. Sources: the way to Birka beset by pirates (Rimbert c. 10); the coast watch against raiders, 'vikinga vordr' (U 617); hired rowers paid at the venture's end (npc_text_encounters.md 1.1, the crew's terms): a master who dies abroad leaves them unpaid. Torkel (invented; a Svea name, U 379). Sets ch_dirham_hoard_7 and one of ch_dirham_hoard_rower_paid, ch_dirham_hoard_rower_owed, ch_dirham_hoard_rower_enemy.

rower.note: Torkel, six summers at the dead man's oar (invented)

cards.title: Six oars
cards.intention: A six-oared boat has come out from behind a skerry and lies across your bow. No sail, no cargo, six men. The one in the stern stands up. You have heard of him twice already.

options.label: Pay him what the dead man owed him: half a mark, weighed over the gunwale
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s07.out_wages

options.label: Heave to, lift the deck boards, and tell him who has the silver
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s07.out_show_success / out_show_failure

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s07.out_run_success / out_run_failure

cards.note: Step 8 (drawn at Paviken in June, July or August, once forty days have passed since step 6: in most games the summer after). The thing. Brother and daughter each claim the lot under the floor, and the stranger who heard the dead man's words is the only witness to them. Sources: the thing decides by the voice of the free men, not by a king (Rimbert c. 26 to 27, of the Svear; peoples/svea_gotlandic.md 3); Gotland has no king and keeps its own law (Guta saga; late); the island's all-thing and its judges are attested only in the 13th-century law (?), so the card says only 'the thing' and 'the man who speaks the law'; a daughter inherits where there are no sons (Guta Lag; late (?)). A man who gave his hand at step 1 cannot speak for the brother. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_8 and one of ch_dirham_hoard_spoke_true, ch_dirham_hoard_spoke_daughter, ch_dirham_hoard_spoke_brother. Schedules step 9.

cards.title: The only witness
cards.intention: The hay is in and the thing has met on the slope above the farms. The bronze bowl stands on a hide in the middle of the ring. Vivil stands on one side of it and Ailikn on the other. An old man who knows the law by heart asks who heard the dead man speak, and every head turns to the Frisian.

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s08.out_daughter (all fifteen marks to Ailikn)

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s08.out_brother (all fifteen marks to the farm; Vivil pays a mark for the word)

cards.note: Step 9, the second turn and the parting of the roads (scheduled by step 8 for the next day; also drawn on any later call at Paviken). The lot under the floor was fifteen marks. The dead man spoke of near forty. The rest lies under the stern stone of an old ship of stones in the east pasture, and only the Frisian knows it (if he swore at step 1, or the stick was read at step 3) or carries the stick that says it. Sources: ship settings of standing stones on Gotland, old already in these years (Bronze Age; Gannarve and others; hoards_793.json's note on Gotland's stone settings); the two lots of Spillings; hoards never recovered by their owners (npc_text_encounters.md 1.5). That a hoard was laid in such a setting is invented. Ottar, Vivil's son (invented; the name from G 113). Sets ch_dirham_hoard_9 and one road: ch_dirham_hoard_road_daughter (to s10), ch_dirham_hoard_road_brother (to s11), ch_dirham_hoard_road_fellowship (to s14, after the timer ch_dirham_hoard_wait_ship, 400 days), ch_dirham_hoard_road_buried (to s12, at once). A house that knows nothing of the second lot has only the last option, and for it the rest is never found: which is how it went.

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_daughter (scheduled by step 9, two days later; also drawn on any later call at Paviken). Ailikn digs at the stern stone before light with the Frisian's men and has twenty-four marks. A third is the finder's; she weighs it out. Sources: women who hold farms and silver in their own right (Frideburg and Catla, Rimbert c. 20; the rune stones U 29, Vs 24; scales in women's graves at Birka (?)); the Gotland farmer-merchants. Grand reward unlock_factor_paviken: a woman with a farm near the beach and silver of her own keeps a foreign house's goods between its calls. On 'peace' a second, unlock_title_gotland_guest_right: the brother's word as well as hers, so the house may winter on the island under two farms' protection. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_end_daughter and ch_dirham_hoard_done; 'third' sets the lasting cost ch_dirham_hoard_brother_bitter; 'peace' sets ch_dirham_hoard_peace.

cards.intention: Before light, at the stern stone, on the seaward side, an arm deep: a second bowl, bigger than the first, sealed with pitch. Ailikn has your scale set up on the fallen stone beside it before the sun is over the trees. Her uncle stands at the pasture fence and comes no nearer.

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s10.out_third

memory.peace: took half his third and made her uncle a gift of the rest

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_brother (scheduled by step 9, two days later; also drawn on any later call at Paviken; closed to a man who swore at step 1). Vivil digs at the stern stone, pays the Frisian five marks and a strip of his shore, and lays the rest back in the ground in a place he tells nobody. Sources: silver in the ground as a farm's store against a bad year, and hoards whose owner died without telling: over 700 on Gotland (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md 5; npc_text_encounters.md 1.5); what a man buries he has after death (Snorri, Ynglinga saga c. 8; late (?)). So this ending too is how it really went: the silver changes holes. Grand reward unlock_plot_paviken: boathouse ground on a farm's shore strip, given by the farmer, which is the only way a stranger gets ground on an island with no town and no king. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_end_brother and ch_dirham_hoard_done; the lasting cost ch_dirham_hoard_daughter_wronged unless the plea for her succeeds (ch_dirham_hoard_peace).

options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s11.out_plead_success / out_plead_failure (it costs only his goodwill)

memory.plead.failure: pressed him for the niece and got nothing

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_buried: what really happened (opened by step 9's last option at once; also drawn on any later call at Paviken). The Frisian stands at the ship of stones in the evening with nobody near, and leaves the silver where the dead man laid it. Twenty-four marks stay under the stern stone until a plough or a stranger finds them, as more than 700 hoards on Gotland stayed. The kin pay him the word-bearer's share of the first lot and give him an arm ring from it, whole. Sources: the hoards of Gotland never recovered (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md 5; economy/silver_coin.md); arm rings made to a weight and worn before they are cut (Spillings); a man has in the next world what he buried himself (Snorri, Ynglinga saga c. 8; late (?)). Grand reward unlock_heirloom_gute_arm_ring: a ring a family gives a stranger is kept, shown and inherited, and is his proof on the island of who he is. On 'stick' a second, unlock_title_gotland_guest_right. The option 'dig' goes to s13 instead and needs the knowledge itself, not the unread stick. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_end_buried and ch_dirham_hoard_done, or ch_dirham_hoard_spade.

cards.intention: The ship of stones lies in the east pasture with its bow to the sea, as it has lain longer than anyone can say. The stern stone is the tallest and leans a little. The turf on its seaward side has not been cut in years. From here you can see the farm's smoke, and nobody can see you.

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_thief (opened by s12's option 'dig'; also drawn at Paviken while ch_dirham_hoard_spade is set). The Frisian digs at the stern stone by night. The danger was told on the card before: the farm's dogs, and what the island does with a stranger found digging. Sources: a stranger off the track who does not shout or blow a horn is taken for a thief (Ine 20; English law, used here only for how any country treats a stranger in the dark); a foreigner's life is priced at ten marks of silver on Gotland against twenty-four for an islander (Guta Lag 15; late); Egil hid his silver with two thralls' help and nobody found it (Egils saga, late). Grand reward unlock_heirloom_stern_stone_ring: a twisted neck ring too well known to sell in the north. The lasting costs: ch_dirham_hoard_feud on 'all' (both kin know by morning whose spade it was), ch_dirham_hoard_secret on 'third' (nobody knows but the crew), and ch_dirham_hoard_oathbreaker is for the integrator to read from ch_dirham_hoard_oath with ch_dirham_hoard_end_thief. 'cover' ends as end_buried. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_done.

hand.note: cast.crew.ravn, or a Norse hand of the forge

brother.note: Vivil (invented); not present: he is here for what he will remember

cards.title: An arm deep
cards.intention: No moon. The spade goes in on the seaward side of the stern stone and an arm down it rings on bronze. The bowl is sealed with pitch and takes two men to lift. Up at the farm a dog has started, stopped, and started again.

options.label: Take all of it and be at sea by first light
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s13.out_all_success / out_all_failure (failing: the dogs are loosed, the bowl is dropped at the fence and one bag reaches the boat)

options.label: Take a finder's third, eight marks and one ring, and lay the turf back over the rest
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s13.out_third (nobody on the island knows; the crew does)

options.label: Look at it, seal it again, and fill the hole
options.note: outcome: chain_dirham_hoard.s13.out_cover (the same end as s12's 'leave': the kin pay the word-bearer's share in the morning and know nothing of the night)

memory.all: dug up the dead man's silver by night and sailed
memory.all.failure: was run off the pasture by the dogs with a bag of the dead man's silver
memory.third: took a third from under the stone and told nobody

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_fellowship: history changed (drawn at Paviken in August, September or October once the timer of step 9 has run out: 400 days, a winter's building and a summer's voyage). Both lots, thirty-nine marks, went into a ship built on the beach instead of back into the ground: Ottar steers her, Ailikn and the farm each hold a share, and the Frisian house holds the third and has a booth of its own above the tide line. Sources: the fellowship of one purse, the felag (the word on 11th-century rune stones, the thing older (?)); Gotland's farmer-merchants who sail east each summer (Guta saga, late; the spine's hook for Paviken); Paviken's shipwrights (ports_793.json); the sea trader of the Askekarr kind, about 16 m (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md 6); foreign merchants are not known to have had ground on Gotland before the Germans of the 12th century (Henry the Lion's peace with the Gotlanders, Artlenburg 1161 (?)). Grand rewards unlock_partner_ottar and unlock_plot_paviken; the changes changed_gotland_hoard_spent and changed_frisians_on_gotland. Sets ch_dirham_hoard_end_fellowship and ch_dirham_hoard_done.

cards.title: Silver that floats
cards.intention: A new ship lies on the beach at Paviken, home from the east three days, her sail of chequered wool spread to dry. Skins are stacked in a new booth above the tide line, and the booth has a Frisian's mark cut over the door. Ottar, Ailikn and Vivil are waiting by the scale. Nobody has dug anything on Aikgard this year except a well.

options.label: Take your third of the voyage, and give your hand on next summer's

options.label: Take your third in silver, keep the booth, and swear to nothing further
